newsitem.title: USA: UPS files suit in Ky. against its pilots.
newsitem.headline: UPS files suit in Ky. against its pilots.

text.p: United Parcel Service on Thursday sued its pilots, accusing them of intimidating pilots of independently chartered planes into not carrying the strike-hit shipper's packages.

The company said it was seeking a temporary restraining order Thursday night in Jefferson County Circuit Court to prevent the 2,000-member Independent Pilots Association from intimidating charter pilots at its half-dozen U.S. hubs.

UPS said it was also seeking a permanent restraining order as well as unspecified damages against its pilots, who have refused to fly the company's planes in an agreement with striking Teamsters not to cross picket lines.

"The pilots are intimidating (the charter pilots), threatening to blacklist them, threatening them with the loss of (airplane) jump-seat privileges ... and other intentional acts," UPS spokesman Ken Shapero said in Louisville.

The union sought to have the case moved to federal court Thursday, but a U.S. District Court judge immediately ordered it back to state court. Jefferson Circuit Judge Ellen Ewing agreed to begin hearing arguments Thursday night.
Union attorney Herb Segal told reporters that the pilots' actions were protected under free speech rights.
Shapero said any restraining order it obtains against its pilots would apply to all its hubs, including its main package hub in Louisville.
On Wednesday, the company chartered six large jets and 30 smaller planes to supplement the 42 company-owned planes being flown by management crews.
The other plaintiffs in the lawsuit were two charter aircraft companies, McMinnville, Ore.-based Evergreen International Aviation Inc. and Burbank, Calif.-based Ameriflight Inc.
Earlier Thursday, Independent Pilots Association President Robert Miller said the pilots could stage a strike of their own near Christmas against UPS.
